info.name: Live Study Room API
info.description:
Single-file Postman collection for the Live Study Room API: auth, profiles, friends, invite-only rooms, join requests, attachments, and Socket.IO notes.

HOW TO USE
1. Import only this file. It carries its own variables, so no environment is required.
2. baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8080 (Docker/nginx). Use http://localhost:3000 only when the API runs directly via npm run dev.
3. Run Setup first. It creates/logs in two demo users (A and B), saves both access tokens, and makes the rest of the collection runnable in one pass.
4. Or run any folder/request on its own. Requests that act as user B already use {{accessTokenB}}; everything else uses the active {{accessToken}}.

TWO USERS
- A = active user (creates rooms, sends the first friend request, approves join requests).
- B = second user (accepts the friend request, accepts invitations, asks to join).
- Change nameA/emailA/passwordA or nameB/emailB/passwordB to use your own accounts.
- Login A also fills {{accessToken}}; Login B fills {{accessTokenB}} and {{userIdB}}.

ROOM FLOWS
- Public room: Create public room -> Join room (as B).
- Invite-only: Create invite-only room -> Invite B -> List invitations (B) -> Accept invitation (B).
- Ask to join: Create join room -> Ask to join (B) -> List requests (A) -> Accept (A).

AUTH NOTES
- Access tokens last 15 minutes. The pre-request script refreshes the active token when it is missing or about to expire.
- The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie, so keep "Send cookies" enabled and use one host consistently (localhost vs 127.0.0.1 are different).
- Refresh and Logout need that cookie. All other requests use the bearer token and work without it.

Socket.IO cannot be exercised from Postman. The client sends the same access token as auth.token. Attachments are uploaded as a base64 data URL, then the returned URL is sent in chat:send.
